name: Sa Talaia — the island's highest point
start: Sant Josep village, church square (free village parking)
blurb: A rural lane past old farmhouses, then pine forest to a bare 475 m summit with a 360° view: Sant Antoni bay, Es Vedrà, the salt pans, Formentera and on clear days Cabrera.
best: Late afternoon for sunset — take a headtorch for the way down in winter.
tip: Sturdy shoes, 1 L water and a windproof layer for the top. Sant Josep council runs a free sunrise walk up here on Sun 15 Nov 2026, 07:15 from the church square.

name: Portinatx → Moscarter lighthouse
start: Portinatx harbour / Platja des Portitxol car park
blurb: Rugged north-coast cliffs to the black-and-white spiral lighthouse of Punta des Moscarter, surf below, and the cove of Cala d'en Serra for a brave winter swim at the end.
best: Morning — the headland is exposed to wind in the afternoon.
tip: Path is rocky and not always obvious: follow the cairns and stay near the coast. 1.5 L water, windbreaker, towel.

name: Cala Llonga → Sol d'en Serra
start: Cala Llonga beach (resort parking)
blurb: A coastal path north through pine and rock, past the Phoenician settlement on Cap des Llibrell, down to the quiet cove of Sol d'en Serra.
best: Any time; lovely light late morning.
tip: Comfortable shoes and swimwear in the shoulder season. Beach cafés may be closed in winter — bring your own.

name: Santa Agnès — Ses Balandres & Ses Portes del Cel
start: Santa Agnès de Corona, village bus stop / church
blurb: Pine forest, the ruins at Ses Balandres and the clifftop natural arch of Ses Portes del Cel. From late January the Pla de Corona almond groves turn white — the island's most photographed winter moment.
best: Late afternoon — the arch is at its best just before sunset. Almond blossom: late Jan to mid-Feb.
tip: Start at the bus stop to avoid village parking trouble. Grippy shoes, 1.5 L water. Afterwards in the village: Can Cosmi opposite the church (open all year, famous tortilla, salsa nights), Sa Palmera for classic Spanish cooking on the square, Es Cucons for lunch, a sauna or a concert (until 15 Nov, back end of Feb), or Las Puertas del Cielo on the cliffs for sunset (until 15 Nov, back end of Feb).

name: Es Portitxol — the hidden horseshoe cove
start: Urbanización Isla Blanca, Cap Blanc road above Port de Sant Miquel
blurb: A cliff path a hundred metres above the sea to a perfect horseshoe cove of traditional fishermen's huts, then a steep climb back through forest, ruins and farmland.
best: Morning, with lunch at the cove.
tip: No facilities at all — bring water and food. The climb out is steep.

name: Cala de Sant Vicent → Punta Grossa
start: Platja de Cala Sant Vicent
blurb: Short but serious: an eroded, scrambly headland path to the ruined lighthouse of Punta Grossa, with views over the north-east coast and Tagomago. Gentler alternative: the Es Culleram Punic cave loop (8.8 km, moderate).
best: Morning, dry conditions only.
tip: Sure-footed walkers only. Sturdy shoes, no phone signal, and mind the deep hole at the ruins.

name: Cala Salada → Cova de ses Fontanelles
start: Cala Salada beach (limited parking) or the bus stop behind Sant Antoni beach
blurb: Pine-shaded hairpins up to the hilltops of Cap Nunó, then a steep drop to a cave with faded Bronze Age paintings and dramatic cliffs. Gorgeous at sunset.
best: Late afternoon.
tip: Little shade on the ridge and no refreshments except the Cala Salada restaurant. Final rock clamber.

name: Cala Bassa → Torre d'en Rovira → Platges de Comte
start: Cala Bassa or Cala Comte car park
blurb: Flat coastal walking past fishermen's huts to the Torre d'en Rovira watchtower, with the islets of Conillera and s'Illa des Bosc offshore. The west coast's classic sunset stroll.
best: The last hour before sunset.
tip: Fully exposed — cap and sunscreen even in winter, plus water.

name: Es Broll de Buscastell
start: Camí des Broll track off the Sant Antoni – Santa Agnès road
blurb: A natural monument: a spring-fed valley of Arab-era irrigation channels, terraces, reeds and vegetable gardens that stays green all winter. Flat, shaded, perfect with kids.
best: Any time; combine with a coffee in Santa Agnès.
tip: Easy shoes. Respect the gardens — they are still worked.

name: Port de Sant Miquel ↔ Benirràs circular
start: Port de Sant Miquel beach
blurb: A proper half-day: Can Marçà cave, clifftop views, the drum-circle beach of Benirràs and forested hills on the way back.
best: Start by 10:00 in winter to be back before dusk.
tip: Carry 2 L water and lunch; swim at Benirràs if the sea is calm.

name: Ses Salines → Torre de ses Portes
area: Sant Josep — Ses Salines Natural Park
start: Platja de ses Salines car park
blurb: Dunes, juniper and the watchtower facing Formentera; extend via Es Cavallet and the salt pans (8 km) to see the flamingos.
best: Golden hour; flamingos are easiest from the salt-pan road.
tip: Sant Josep council runs a free full-moon walk here on Sat 23 Jan 2027 at 18:15. Visit the Sant Francesc interpretation centre.

name: Santa Eulària river walk & Puig de Missa
start: Santa Eulària waterfront
blurb: Paved riverside path with a small waterfall, the old watermill, the padlock bridge and the Roman Pont Vell, climbing to the 16th-century fortified church on Puig de Missa. Pushchair-friendly for most of it.
best: Sunday morning before the market crowds.
tip: Ideal with kids; coffee stops all along the paseo.

name: Dalt Vila walls & bastions
start: Portal de ses Taules, Ibiza Town
blurb: The UNESCO walls, seven bastions, the cathedral and the marina — three official routes (Classic, Bastions, Unknown) in a free PDF from the tourist board.
best: Late afternoon light on the ramparts.
tip: Cobbles — no heels. Ends perfectly at a harbour-front café.

name: Es Plans — the almond-blossom loop
start: Sant Antoni (or anywhere on the loop)
blurb: Road loop over the plains of Corona and Sant Mateu to Santa Gertrudis and back via Buscastell. One of the Consell's signposted routes — at its best in February when the almond trees flower.
best: Feb–Mar for the blossom; mornings any time.
tip: Rolling, not brutal. Coffee stop in Santa Gertrudis.

name: Es Vedrà road loop
start: Sant Josep village
blurb: The south-west classic: Sant Josep's coves, Es Cubells and the Es Vedrà viewpoints, with proper climbs. Experienced road riders.
best: Early start; sunset views on the return.
tip: Bike hire from around €30/day in Ibiza Town or Sant Antoni.

name: Es Pobles — village to village
start: Any village on the loop (Santa Gertrudis is a good base)
blurb: Sant Miquel, Sant Llorenç, Santa Gertrudis, Sant Mateu, Sant Antoni and Corona in one ride — every white church on the island's quiet inland roads.
best: A full winter Saturday.
tip: Carry food; villages close for siesta.

name: Ses Salines flat ride
start: Ibiza Town
blurb: Platja d'en Bossa, the salt pans, Es Cavallet, Cap des Falcó and back past Dalt Vila. Flat, scenic, beginner- and family-friendly (older kids).
best: Sunday morning.
tip: Watch for flamingos on the salt pans; gravel sections suit a hybrid or gravel bike.

name: Santa Gertrudis – Es Broll gravel loop
start: Santa Gertrudis church square
blurb: MTB/gravel loop through the island's green heart: Es Broll spring, the Santa Eulària river valley and Sa Font de Cotella.
best: After rain the valley is at its greenest.
tip: Gravel or MTB tyres; muddy patches in winter.

name: Cala Sant Vicent → Cala Xarraca → Sant Joan
start: Cala Sant Vicent
blurb: A short, scenic north-coast road ride with one real climb out of Cala Sant Vicent and a coffee reward in Sant Joan.
best: Sunday, then the Sant Joan market.
tip: Combine with the Es Culleram cave visit.

name: Talamanca – harbour – Dalt Vila – Botafoc
start: Ibiza harbour (Café Mar y Sol)
blurb: Flat promenades around the harbour and out to the Botafoc lighthouse, with an optional climb through Dalt Vila. A free social group run leaves Café Mar y Sol on Saturday mornings from October to June.
best: Saturday 09:00 with the group.
tip: Shorter 8 km and longer 12.7 km variants on the same loop.

name: Ses Salines → Torre de ses Portes trail run
area: Sant Josep — Ses Salines Natural Park
start: Platja de ses Salines car park
blurb: Soft sand and pine-needle trail to the watchtower and back; extend onto the salt-pan tracks for 10 km+.
best: Sunrise.
tip: Trail shoes; the sand section is slow.

name: Santa Eulària paseo & river path
start: Santa Eulària beach promenade
blurb: Two kilometres of flat seafront, then the river path to Puig de Missa for a hill finish. The town's uphill race, the Pujada Puig de Missa, is held each January.
best: Early morning.
tip: Fountains along the paseo; cafés open year-round.
